papers.title: Concisely Explaining the Doubt: Minimum-Size Abductive Explanations for Linear Models with a Reject Option
papers.venue: XAI 2026 (4th World Conference on eXplainable Artificial Intelligence); arXiv:2603.14096
papers.authors: Gleilson Pedro Fernandes, Thiago Alves Rocha
papers.why: Closest single paper to CertGate component (4): computes provably minimal abductive explanations of WHY a linear classifier with a reject option rejected an instance (0-1 ILP formulation), motivated by healthcare/finance oversight. Same object (linear model + reject + faithful explanation of the rejection) but no statistical certificate, no cluster/site structure, no clinical validation. A reviewer in this lane would expect it cited next to CertGate's exact linear abstention attributions.

papers.title: Interpretable and Fair Mechanisms for Abstaining Classifiers (IFAC)
papers.venue: ECML PKDD 2024 (Machine Learning and Knowledge Discovery in Databases, Springer LNCS); arXiv:2503.18826
papers.authors: Daphne Lenders, Andrea Pugnana, Roberto Pellungrini, Toon Calders, Dino Pedreschi, Fosca Giannotti
papers.why: Abstaining classifier whose rejections are interpretable by construction (rule-based fairness checks + situation testing), so a human can see why each prediction was withheld. Overlaps the explainable-abstention component directly; no finite-sample answered-error certificate, no site-as-unit statistics, fairness-driven rather than error-driven abstention.

papers.title: "I do not know! but why?" — Local model-agnostic example-based explanations of reject
papers.authors: Andre Artelt, Roel Visser, Barbara Hammer
papers.why: The mature statement of the Hammer-group program on explaining reject options: model-agnostic, example-based (counterfactual/semi-factual/factual) explanations of why an instance was rejected. Companion works include 'Even if...' diverse semifactual explanations of reject (IEEE SSCI 2022) and Model Agnostic Local Explanations of Reject (ESANN 2022, arXiv:2205.07623). This corpus defines the lane; CertGate differs by exact linear attributions tied to a certified gate rather than post-hoc example-based explanation, but the related-work section needs this line of work.

papers.title: Explaining Reject Options of Learning Vector Quantization Classifiers
papers.venue: ICAART 2022 (14th International Conference on Agents and Artificial Intelligence); arXiv:2202.07244
papers.authors: Andre Artelt, Johannes Brinkrolf, Roel Visser, Barbara Hammer
papers.why: Earlier classic of the same program: efficient counterfactual explanations of the reject options of prototype-based (LVQ) classifiers. Establishes that explaining rejects was an open problem with very little prior work — useful positioning citation for CertGate's abstention-attribution layer.

papers.title: Machine learning with a reject option: a survey
papers.authors: Kilian Hendrickx, Lorenzo Perini, Dries Van der Plas, Wannes Meert, Jesse Davis
papers.why: The canonical 2024 survey of reject-option ML (ambiguity vs novelty rejection; confidence-based vs classifier-rejector architectures). Not itself about explanation or certification, but it is the reference frame reviewers will use to place CertGate's gate, and its taxonomy (record-level, i.i.d.) is exactly what CertGate's site-as-unit treatment departs from.

papers.title: Model Agnostic Explainable Selective Regression via Uncertainty Estimation
papers.authors: Andrea Pugnana, Carlos Mougan, Dan Saattrup Nielsen
papers.why: Explicitly uses XAI techniques to identify the drivers behind selective abstention (in regression) — the same question CertGate's E5 'abstention driver' analysis asks. Model-agnostic post-hoc explanation over uncertainty-based abstention; no finite-sample certificate, no cluster structure, no clinical data.

papers.title: Knowing What You Cannot Explain: Learning to Reject Low-Quality Explanations (REX)
papers.authors: Luca Stradiotti, Dario Pesenti, Stefano Teso, Jesse Davis
papers.why: Couples explanation and rejection in the INVERSE direction: abstain when the model cannot produce a satisfactory explanation, rather than explain why it abstained. A reviewer scanning 'explanation + abstention' will surface it; CertGate should distinguish its direction (explanations OF abstention, under a certificate) from REX's (abstention BECAUSE OF explanations).

papers.title: Deferring Concept Bottleneck Models: Learning to Defer Interventions to Inaccurate Experts
papers.why: Interpretable deferral via concept bottlenecks: the system can defer instance-wise or concept-wise, so the deferral decision is grounded in human-understandable concepts — the L2D-side analogue of explainable abstention. Consistent surrogate-loss guarantees but no finite-sample answered-error certificate and no cluster-as-unit statistics.

papers.title: Learning to Defer: A Survey
papers.authors: Joshua Strong, Emma Sun, Harry Rogers, Helen Higham
papers.why: Four-branch taxonomy of the learning-to-defer literature, listing interpretability and uncertainty handling among open practical considerations — confirms explanation-of-deferral is recognized as open, and useful for positioning CertGate's abstention layer against the L2D framing without claiming to solve L2D.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning with reject option
papers.why: The earliest explicit pairing of interpretable models (LVQ) with reject options — the classic the authors may have missed if they only cite 2022+ work; roots the claim that interpretability and abstention have been combined before, though without explanation of individual rejects or any statistical certificate.

papers.title: L2D-Clinical: Learning to Defer for Adaptive Model Selection in Clinical Text Classification
papers.why: Recent clinical deferral system (BERT defers to an LLM) that advertises 'interpretable, task-specific patterns about when deferral helps'; abstract-level check shows the interpretability claim is thin (uncertainty signals + text characteristics, no per-case explanation). Context for clinical deferral, not a threat to CertGate's combination.

papers.title: Selective Omniprediction and Fair Abstention
papers.why: Theory of selective prediction with abstention under fairness/omniprediction constraints — shows where the theory community is taking abstention semantics, but no explanation layer, no cluster-as-unit certification, no clinical component.

collision_verdict: No COLLISION found in this lane. Nothing located combines site/cluster-as-unit finite-sample certification of answered-set error with an explanation layer for abstention; the lane's closest work (Fernandes & Rocha 2026; IFAC 2024; the Artelt/Hammer corpus) explains or structures individual rejections without any statistical certificate, and the certified-abstention literature surfaced in adjacent searches carries no explanation layer and is record-i.i.d.
